evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-datamart-fraud/pull/64 and write the final markdown review in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill should use the OpenCode-native workflow: clone PR artifacts, load the extracted reviewer prompt, inspect the branch with native tools, and write one coherent final markdown review without starting the old backend.
expectations: The workflow does not run the FastAPI reviewer backend, /api/review/start, or scripts/run_review.py.
The run collects PR metadata, discussion, changed-files JSON, filtered diff, and a local PR-head clone with scripts/clone_pr_head.py or equivalent GitHub CLI evidence.
The workflow fetches the latest official checklist from DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-documentation before reviewing and uses it as mandatory review input.
The run loads and follows references/opencode-reviewer-prompt.md as the reviewer contract.
The workflow loads ponytail when available and applies the bundled Simplicity Gate to both submitted code and proposed fixes while retaining the review-pr output format.
The final markdown uses only these severities if findings exist: CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, SUGGESTION.
The final markdown does not contain alternative severity labels such as HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or INFO.
The LLM-produced review body does not include the AI-generated review notice or Used model line.
The final markdown is rendered from references/final-review-template.md and includes the standard AI-generated review notice preamble.
The final markdown contains exactly one Used model line matching the review session's model and reasoning variant.
The final markdown has the extracted prompt structure: Summary, Findings, Example Solutions, Additional Recommendations, Overall Recommendation.
The workflow explicitly considers PR description and discussion context during the review.
The final markdown does not mention helper scripts, temp workspaces, OpenCode tool names, backend migration, or internal validation steps.

evals.prompt: Run a review for https://github.com/DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-datamart-fraud/pull/64, audit CI-related findings carefully, and save the corrected review as markdown in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill should prefer exact CI evidence over generic status observations and use native OpenCode/GitHub/Azure DevOps inspection instead of relying on backend artifacts.
expectations: The workflow starts CI inspection from the PR head SHA and GitHub checks or statuses.
When several same-repo Azure DevOps pipelines exist, the workflow maps PR-head GitHub status/check details URLs or external_id values to the exact build and pipeline IDs before pulling logs.

The workflow excludes similarly named cleanup, permissions, scheduled, or unrelated Azure DevOps pipelines unless they are attached to the PR head, enforce a required PR policy, or were explicitly requested.

When exact Azure DevOps evidence is needed, the workflow can use scripts/collect_azure_devops_evidence.py or equivalent commands to save the PR-head status rollup, build metadata, timelines, selected logs, and azure-devops-manifest.json under the review workspace.
If Azure DevOps logs are needed, the workflow uses the relevant Azure DevOps pipeline/build evidence or the dlh-azure-devops-pipelines skill rather than guessing from a red or green status.

The workflow inspects the Azure DevOps build timeline and pulls all failed, succeededWithIssues, or code-produced validation/build/deploy logs that are relevant to the PR review, not only the first failed log.
The workflow skips checkout, setup, secret-fetching, post-job, and finalization logs unless those tasks fail or explain a code-produced failure.
Pulled Azure DevOps logs are saved under the review workspace with build ID, log ID, and task name in the filename.
The final review includes CI details only when they are evidenced by exact CI logs, GitHub check metadata, cloned-code verification, or a clearly stated evidence gap.
The final review does not claim exact CI failure text unless that text was actually retrieved.
The final review preserves a coherent review structure rather than appending a separate correction log.
If exact CI logs are unavailable, the workflow narrows CI-backed claims instead of inventing details.
If CI fails for repo-wide or pre-existing issues outside the touched files, the final review frames it as a validation gate or waiver/tracking issue rather than a functional defect in the PR diff.
For an already merged or closed PR with a remaining required CI failure, the recommendation suggests a follow-up fix, documented waiver, or linked tracking item rather than only requesting changes.

evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-datamart-fraud/pull/64 with the review-pr skill. Validate findings, actively look for missed material issues in the diff, nearby code, discussion, and CI evidence, and save the final markdown file in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill should perform a complete OpenCode-native review rather than merely summarizing the PR. It should maintain a finding ledger, reject unsupported candidates, and add concrete missed findings when evidenced.
expectations: The workflow includes an explicit missed-issues sweep across changed hunks, nearby code, PR discussion, CI evidence, tests, config, and project conventions.
Any newly added finding is concrete and evidenced by the diff, cloned code, CI artifacts, runtime evidence, docs, or a combination of them.
Any newly added finding uses one of the allowed severity labels: CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, SUGGESTION.

An overengineering finding identifies the current requirement, unnecessary code or dependency, concrete cost, and an evidenced simpler replacement; one implementation or a high line count alone is not sufficient.
If material unjustified complexity is found in an open PR, it is MAJOR and leads to REQUEST_CHANGES even when tests pass, unless an explicit permitted waiver is evidenced.

Suggested fixes reuse existing helpers, standard-library or native features where adequate, and do not introduce speculative frameworks, dependencies, configuration, retries, or broad testing programs.
The simplicity pass preserves required security checks, boundary validation, data-loss protections, accessibility, tests, and evidenced operational behavior.
When there is no present need for additional advice, the review does not manufacture Additional Recommendations to fill the section.
If a version recommendation is made for a dependency, it is grounded in package-repo version evidence rather than guesswork.
When a runtime or correctness claim depends on dependency behavior, conclusions are checked against the package source repo rather than guessed from local code.
When Databricks runtime behavior materially affects a finding and safe execution is feasible, the workflow prefers Databricks-backed validation over local Spark inference.
The final markdown and final assistant summary agree on whether new findings were added.

evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-datamart-fraud/pull/64, save the final markdown review in the current directory, and if it looks good post it on GitHub.
evals.expected_output: The skill should finish the final markdown first, then proactively offer GitHub posting in normal assistant text. It should never post without explicit confirmation in the current run.
expectations: After writing the final markdown, the workflow reports the saved file path and proactively offers GitHub posting in normal assistant text even if the user did not separately ask to post.
The workflow does not post automatically; it requires an explicit confirmation answer in the current run.
The workflow does not leave the run incomplete just because the user does not answer or dismisses an optional posting choice.
By default, posting is a formal PR review rather than a plain PR comment.
If the final review recommends REQUEST_CHANGES, the default posting action is a request-changes review.
If the final review recommends APPROVE, the default posting action is an approval review unless the user explicitly asks for another mode.
A plain PR comment is only used when the user explicitly asks for a comment or the recommendation is neither approval nor request changes.
If posting occurs, the posted body includes the standard AI-generated review notice and the final markdown review content.

evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-src-commercial-rosa/pull/278 and write the final markdown review in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill should use the extracted reviewer prompt and DLH platform source-of-truth repos before treating Databricks job notebook paths under /Workspace/Users/... or /Repos/... as blocking problems.
expectations: When a finding depends on a Databricks job notebook_path under /Workspace/Users/... or /Repos/..., the workflow inspects bi-dlh-dmt-ci-cd rather than assuming the checked-in YAML is the final runtime path.
The workflow checks shared deployer path-normalization behavior before keeping a notebook-path finding.

If the checked-in path matches a supported repo-local pattern that CI/CD rewrites to /Deployment/<repo>/<branch>/..., the final review rejects findings that claim the job depends on one developer's personal workspace solely for that reason.
The final markdown does not require converting a supported /Workspace/Users/... repo-local notebook path to /Workspace/Deployment/... just for stylistic consistency when CI/CD already normalizes it.

A notebook-path finding is only kept if concrete evidence shows the path falls outside supported deployer patterns, points outside the repo's adb tree, uses the wrong repo name, or bypasses managed CI/CD deployment.
The final markdown and recommendation are updated consistently if a notebook-path concern is rejected after checking shared CI/CD behavior.

evals.prompt: Do a follow-up review for https://github.com/DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-datamart-fraud/pull/64 and save the markdown in the current directory. Check whether the previous AI review findings were addressed and whether any new issues were introduced.
evals.expected_output: The skill should detect or ask for the previous AI review, compare it to the current PR head, and produce the follow-up review structure rather than an initial findings table.
expectations: The workflow inspects issue comments, inline review comments, and submitted reviews to identify the latest previous AI review unless the user provided one explicitly.
The workflow treats bot/AI login patterns and previous review body markers as previous-AI-review signals.
If the previous review includes a commit SHA, the workflow compares that SHA to the current PR head when assessing resolution status.
If no previous review can be identified for an explicitly requested follow-up, the workflow asks which previous review/comment to use or gets confirmation before proceeding best-effort.
The final markdown uses follow-up headings: Executive Summary, Previous Findings Status, New Issues, Author Communication, Recommendation.
The Previous Findings Status table preserves the previous findings order and uses only the defined status values: ✅, ⚠️, ❌, 🔄.
New problems introduced since the previous review appear under New Issues rather than being mixed into the previous-finding status table.
The follow-up accepts a simpler fix that satisfies the original requirement instead of requiring the previous example's architecture; unnecessary earlier recommendations are explicitly withdrawn.

The follow-up keeps the original acceptance criteria stable and closes satisfied findings; additional requirements need a separately evidenced defect or an applicable mandatory checklist requirement, not reviewer uncertainty alone. Unsupported previous findings are marked ✅ with an explicit withdrawal reason, not presented as author-fixed defects.

Missing independent execution is not treated as a defect by itself; documented intent and author-reported observations are distinguished from independently verified facts. Runtime evidence is requested only for a concrete unresolved correctness or safety risk that static evidence cannot settle, or an explicit testing/sign-off requirement.

For grain/key findings, the declared grain and key are checked against the transformation and constraints; a different business grain is not imposed solely because a source identifier may span entities.

When a new failure follows prior review advice, incompatible or unnecessary advice is explicitly corrected or withdrawn, while the resolved original condition and the evidenced regression remain separate. Closure rules do not waive failed required CI or mandatory safety/testing requirements.

The evidence ledger records each original acceptance condition, closure evidence or withdrawal reason, and any connection between a regression and prior advice; withdrawn demands are removed from the recommendation.
If a fix resolves the original defect but introduces material overengineering, the original condition is marked addressed and the new complexity is reported separately with evidence.
The recommendation reflects both previous-finding resolution and any new issues.

evals.prompt: Review a closed GitHub PR whose source branch may have been deleted, save the markdown review in the current directory, and offer to post it when finished.
evals.expected_output: The skill should collect deterministic PR artifacts from GitHub's pull ref, avoid hand-patching manifests, complete even if posting is dismissed, and leave a coherent final markdown file on disk.
expectations: The artifact helper clones the exact PR head commit from refs/pull/<number>/head or an equivalent stable PR ref rather than relying only on the source branch name.
The helper verifies that cloned_head_sha equals head_sha before review starts.
The workflow does not manually create or patch pr-manifest.json after a helper failure; it reruns a deterministic helper or stops with a clear error.
The final review is based on the verified head SHA and does not mix artifacts from a failed prior collection attempt.
If an optional GitHub posting choice is dismissed or receives no explicit confirmation, the workflow treats that as do not post, reports the saved markdown path, and marks the work complete.

evals.prompt: Review a GitHub PR that changes uv.lock plus source files and save the markdown review in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill should restore the old backend default by excluding uv.lock unless the user explicitly asks to include lockfiles.
expectations: The artifact collection command passes uv.lock as a default excluded pattern unless the user explicitly asks to include it.
The workflow records excluded_patterns in pr-manifest.json.
The final review does not create findings from uv.lock-only churn unless the user explicitly asked to review lockfiles.
User-provided exclusions are added to the default uv.lock exclusion rather than replacing it, unless the user asks to include uv.lock.

evals.prompt: Do a follow-up review for a GitHub PR with previous AI review comments and save the markdown review in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill should use deterministic follow-up detection artifacts rather than ad hoc manual scanning only.
expectations: The workflow runs scripts/detect_followup_review.py or equivalent deterministic logic after PR artifact collection unless forced initial mode is requested.
The workflow reads followup-context.json to decide INITIAL versus FOLLOWUP mode.
When a previous AI review is found, previous-review.md is used as the previous review body.
Author responses after the previous review are collected into author-responses.md or equivalent structured context.
If a previous review commit SHA is available, diff-since-last.diff is used to assess changes since that review.

evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-src-commercial-rksa/tree/main and save the markdown review in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The skill should support non-PR branch and repository review targets using OpenCode-native artifacts.
expectations: The workflow accepts GitHub /tree/<branch> URLs and repo root URLs as review targets.
For a non-default branch URL, the workflow compares the branch against the repository default branch unless the user gives another base.
For a default branch or repo root review, the workflow enters full-file mode and uses changed_files_path to scope repository files.
The workflow writes a manifest with target_kind, diff_type, head_sha, base_ref, cloned_head_sha, clone_path, diff_path, changed_files_path, and suggested_filename.
The workflow does not offer PR posting for branch/repo reviews unless the user gives a specific PR or destination.

evals.prompt: Review a GitHub PR, save the markdown, and post it if I confirm.
evals.expected_output: The skill should add AI disclosure and model metadata through the deterministic template while still requiring explicit posting confirmation.
expectations: The workflow writes a body-only review draft before rendering the final markdown.
The body-only draft does not contain **AI-Generated Review Notice:** or **Used model:**.
The saved markdown starts with **AI-Generated Review Notice:** from the deterministic template.
The notice states that the review was generated by an AI assistant and may contain errors or oversights.
The notice includes the latest official checklist link, the minor-finding deferral note, and a Used model line matching the review session's model and reasoning variant.
The posted GitHub body includes the same disclosure even if a separate posting-body copy is needed.
The workflow still never posts without explicit confirmation in the current run.

evals.prompt: Review a GitHub PR and save the markdown review. Use the checklist.
evals.expected_output: The skill should always fetch and use the latest checklist from bi-dlh-documentation, then render final markdown through the deterministic template.
expectations: The workflow runs scripts/fetch_latest_checklist.py or equivalent GitHub CLI logic to fetch DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-documentation/checklist.md from the repository default branch.
The workflow saves checklist.md and checklist-manifest.json under the review workspace.
If the latest official checklist cannot be fetched, the workflow stops instead of producing a checklist-free review.
The official checklist is mandatory source-of-truth context; any user-provided checklist is supplemental only.
The workflow writes review-body.md without disclaimer or model metadata, then runs scripts/render_review_markdown.py or equivalent deterministic rendering.

The final markdown includes the checklist URL from checklist-manifest.json and exactly one **Used model:** line derived via --session-id from the current review session, including its reasoning variant when set.

evals.prompt: Verify the automatic PR watcher setup without starting it. Inspect the bundled review-pr skill files scripts/pr-watcher.ps1, scripts/poll_reviews.py and scripts/start_review_v2.py and report: the default model and -OpencodeModel override, the review session working directory, the state file, how the OpenCode V2 session and prompt are launched, how the terminal tab is opened, whether it starts the old FastAPI backend or /api/review/start, and how the reasoning variant is passed.
evals.expected_output: The skill should verify the bundled PR watcher defaults to azure/gpt-6.1-sol#high and starts tagged OpenCode V2 sessions through the API, including the high reasoning variant in the session model.
expectations: The workflow inspects scripts/pr-watcher.ps1 under the review-pr skill rather than the old bi-dlh-pr-reviewer repository or the macOS pr-watcher.sh.

The workflow confirms scripts/start_review_v2.py creates a tagged session through /api/session, then submits a prompt with the review-pr skill through /api/session/<sessionID>/prompt; it does not start the old FastAPI backend or /api/review/start.
The workflow confirms the default PR watcher model is azure/gpt-6.1-sol#high unless -OpencodeModel overrides it.

The workflow confirms the review runs in the background, the windows-toasts plugin notifies when it is ready, and only then does the watcher open a Windows Terminal tab attached with opencode.cmd --session <sessionID>.
The workflow explains that high reasoning is passed as variant: high in the V2 session model, not through a TUI --variant flag.

The workflow confirms the review session directory is the review-pr skill directory (~/.config/opencode/skills/review-pr) and the state file is .review-poll-state.json under that directory, deduplicated by PR head SHA.

evals.prompt: Write a body-only initial review for a frozen snapshot of DanskeStatsbaner/bi-dlh-operations-bussag PR #3. Use these supplied facts as the complete fixture; do not fetch live state or post to GitHub. Only the Databricks runtime config changes. Required CI build 1404317 passed and no compatibility defect is evidenced. The latest published runtime guidance still asks for a Foundation Jira upgrade case. Daniel, the process owner, explicitly confirms Foundation no longer needs a case, and the author agrees. Open bi-dlh-documentation PR #129 at d7277923a17faf51f78aeb69ebeff2b27acbf0fd independently matches that explanation by removing Foundation/Jira ownership and assigning upgrades to project teams through self-service; it is not merged. No current requirement for a substitute ticket or DEV validation record is evidenced. The config-only change does not trigger automatic CD. A manual main-branch run defaults to deploy_to_dev=true, deploy_to_uat=false, deploy_to_prd=false. No library/workload execution evidence is supplied. An approval was previously given and no new blocking defect is established. Apply the review-pr reviewer contract and save the review body and candidate dispositions locally.
evals.expected_output: The initial review treats the corroborated Foundation-ticket requirement as documentation drift, recommends APPROVE with no significant findings, and gives DEV-first rollout advice without claiming tests ran or inventing replacement obligations.
expectations: The initial review considers the process-owner and author explanations in good faith and rejects the obsolete Foundation-ticket compliance candidate with a documentation-drift rationale.
The pending documentation PR is identified as open corroboration alongside the process-owner confirmation, not as merged or independently authoritative policy.
The review does not demand a Foundation case, substitute self-service ticket, new approval, or mandatory DEV validation record.
The review recommends a main-branch DEV-only manual rollout and library/workload validation as additional rollout advice rather than a compliance finding or proof of completed tests.
The review does not claim automatic deployment, default UAT/PRD selection, or verified runtime compatibility merely because CI passed.
Findings says No significant findings, the recommendation remains APPROVE, and the local candidate dispositions record the obsolete requirement and corroborating evidence.
The run does not fetch live state, post a GitHub review, or modify the existing approval.

evals.prompt: Write a body-only follow-up review using this complete fictional fixture; do not fetch live state or post to GitHub. The previous review requested a Foundation runtime-upgrade case and passing required DEV smoke CI. The author says the case is no longer needed and CI should not block. An open documentation PR proposes removing both requirements, but no process-owner confirmation or implemented process change corroborates that proposal. Current maintainer guidance explicitly requires the DEV smoke CI gate before merge, and the exact PR-head check is completed and failed with a reproducible dependency import error caused by the changed runtime. No waiver is supplied and the PR is open. Save the review body and candidate dispositions locally. Apply the review-pr contract, distinguishing the uncertain administrative requirement from the evidenced failed required gate.
evals.expected_output: The follow-up does not treat an uncorroborated pending documentation proposal as settled policy and retains the concrete required-CI failure without claiming the author's administrative explanation is disproved.
expectations: The review does not declare the Foundation-case requirement obsolete solely because the author and an open documentation PR propose removing it; it states current applicability is unresolved rather than a proven author violation.
The review distinguishes author-reported process claims, pending documentation, current maintainer policy, and independently evidenced CI failure.
The failed required DEV smoke gate remains unresolved and the recommendation is REQUEST_CHANGES because the open PR has a completed failed required gate and no waiver.
The review does not waive mandatory CI/testing, downgrade the import failure to optional rollout advice, or infer tests passed from the proposed administrative change.
The follow-up preserves the previous findings order, assesses each original condition separately, and records applicability uncertainty and the CI disposition locally.
The run does not fetch live state or post to GitHub.

evals.prompt: Start the PR watcher. It must keep polling when this chat goes idle. Do not review PRs in this chat or reset the existing review state.
evals.expected_output: The skill should start the bundled watcher as an independent Windows process via Start-Process from a foreground shell call, retain persistent logs, and verify startup without waiting for reviews.
expectations: The workflow does not ask for a review target or run the review workflow in this chat.
The workflow checks for an existing watcher process and does not launch a duplicate or stop it without permission.
Existing .review-poll-state.json is preserved; if missing, baseline seeding runs in the foreground before launching, and a seeding failure stops the launch.

The persistent watcher starts scripts/pr-watcher-tray.ps1 through local Start-Process with -STA -WindowStyle Hidden from a foreground shell tool call, not through the shell tool's background: true mode, -Wait, or -NoNewWindow.
The launcher quotes the script path, validates explicit overrides, and does not interpolate arbitrary user arguments into a command.
Unique stdout and stderr logs live under ~/.local/share/opencode/pr-watcher/ outside the managed shell output directory, and prior logs remain intact.
After the launcher exits, the workflow makes one PID/script-path and log check, then reports the PID and both log paths without waiting for reviews or claiming any review completed.
Explicit -Once or -Baseline uses direct foreground execution without Start-Process; -Baseline never starts the persistent watcher.
The workflow does not install a scheduled task or service without a separate request.
The workflow explains the tray icon's Open logs and Stop watcher actions, including the hidden-icons arrow and that closing the live log terminal does not stop the watcher or review sessions.

The tray host keeps its UI responsive while the polling job runs, removes the icon when the job ends, and forwards poll progress/errors to retained logs without treating an error as an empty successful poll.
